glosses: to reproach, to upbraid, to blame

examples.text: В глаза́ она́ его́ никогда́ не упрека́ла, но укра́дкой жа́ловалась на него́ поочерё́дно всем в до́ме, да́же до́чери.
examples.translation: She had never reproached him to his face, but she complained of him secretly to every one in the house in turn, even to her daughter.
examples.english: She had never reproached him to his face, but she complained of him secretly to every one in the house in turn, even to her daughter.

examples.text: На каждом собрании меня упрекают, тычут под нос даты.

glosses: A mild rebuke, or an implied criticism.

examples.text: My father made no reproach in his letters and only took notice of my science by inquiring into my occupations more particularly than before.

glosses: To disgrace, or bring shame upon.

examples.text: I thought your marriage fit; else imputation, / For that he knew you, might reproach your life.

glosses: To charge with something wrong or disgraceful; to reproach

examples.text: Yet do not upbraid us our distress.

glosses: To object or urge as a matter of reproach

examples.text: Those that have been bred together, are more apt to envy their equals when raised: for it doth upbraid unto them their own fortunes, and pointeth at them.

glosses: The act of reproaching; scorn; disdain.

examples.text:
